From 1015c27a5e1a63efae2b18a9901494474b4d1dc3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 22:10:32 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] USB: core: Limit the length of unkillable synchronous
 timeouts

The usb_control_msg(), usb_bulk_msg(), and usb_interrupt_msg() APIs in
usbcore allow unlimited timeout durations.  And since they use
uninterruptible waits, this leaves open the possibility of hanging a
task for an indefinitely long time, with no way to kill it short of
unplugging the target device.

To prevent this sort of problem, enforce a maximum limit on the length
of these unkillable timeouts.  The limit chosen here, somewhat
arbitrarily, is 60 seconds.  On many systems (although not all) this
is short enough to avoid triggering the kernel's hung-task detector.

In addition, clear up the ambiguity of negative timeout values by
treating them the same as 0, i.e., using the maximum allowed timeout.

Signed-off-by: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-usb/3acfe838-6334-4f6d-be7c-4bb01704b33d@rowland.harvard.edu/
Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/15fc9773-a007-47b0-a703-df89a8cf83dd@rowland.harvard.edu
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/include/linux/usb.h b/include/linux/usb.h
index 57ceeb02a7cb..04277af4bb9d 100644
--- a/include/linux/usb.h
+++ b/include/linux/usb.h
@@ -1862,6 +1862,9 @@ void usb_free_noncoherent(struct usb_device *dev, size_t size,
  *                         SYNCHRONOUS CALL SUPPORT                  *
  *-------------------------------------------------------------------*/
 
+/* Maximum value allowed for timeout in synchronous routines below */
+#define USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT		60000	/* ms */
+
 extern int usb_control_msg(struct usb_device *dev, unsigned int pipe,
 	__u8 request, __u8 requesttype, __u16 value, __u16 index,
 	void *data, __u16 size, int timeout);
--

diff --git a/drivers/usb/core/message.c b/drivers/usb/core/message.c
index d97ec7e8c280..2ab120ce2fa8 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/core/message.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/core/message.c
@@ -45,6 +45,8 @@ static void usb_api_blocking_completion(struct urb *urb)
  * Starts urb and waits for completion or timeout.
  * Whether or not the wait is killable depends on the flag passed in.
  * For example, compare usb_bulk_msg() and usb_bulk_msg_killable().
+ *
+ * For non-killable waits, we enforce a maximum limit on the timeout value.
  */
 static int usb_start_wait_urb(struct urb *urb, int timeout, int *actual_length,
 		bool killable)
@@ -61,7 +63,9 @@ static int usb_start_wait_urb(struct urb *urb, int timeout, int *actual_length,
 	if (unlikely(retval))
 		goto out;
 
-	expire = timeout ? msecs_to_jiffies(timeout) : MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT;
+	if (!killable && (timeout <= 0 || timeout > USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT))
+		timeout = USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT;
+	expire = (timeout > 0) ? msecs_to_jiffies(timeout) : MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT;
 	if (killable)
 		rc = wait_for_completion_killable_timeout(&ctx.done, expire);
 	else
@@ -127,8 +131,7 @@ static int usb_internal_control_msg(struct usb_device *usb_dev,
  * @index: USB message index value
  * @data: pointer to the data to send
  * @size: length in bytes of the data to send
- * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing
- *	out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out
  *
  * Context: task context, might sleep.
  *
@@ -183,8 +186,7 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(usb_control_msg);
  * @index: USB message index value
  * @driver_data: pointer to the data to send
  * @size: length in bytes of the data to send
- * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing
- *	out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out
  * @memflags: the flags for memory allocation for buffers
  *
  * Context: !in_interrupt ()
@@ -242,8 +244,7 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(usb_control_msg_send);
  * @index: USB message index value
  * @driver_data: pointer to the data to be filled in by the message
  * @size: length in bytes of the data to be received
- * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing
- *	out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out
  * @memflags: the flags for memory allocation for buffers
  *
  * Context: !in_interrupt ()
@@ -314,8 +315,7 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(usb_control_msg_recv);
  * @len: length in bytes of the data to send
  * @actual_length: pointer to a location to put the actual length transferred
  *	in bytes
- * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before
- *	timing out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out
  *
  * Context: task context, might sleep.
  *
@@ -347,8 +347,7 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(usb_interrupt_msg);
  * @len: length in bytes of the data to send
  * @actual_length: pointer to a location to put the actual length transferred
  *	in bytes
- * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before
- *	timing out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out
  *
  * Context: task context, might sleep.
  *
@@ -408,12 +407,12 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(usb_bulk_msg);
  * @actual_length: pointer to a location to put the actual length transferred
  *	in bytes
  * @timeout: time in msecs to wait for the message to complete before
- *	timing out (if 0 the wait is forever)
+ *	timing out (if <= 0, the wait is as long as possible)
  *
  * Context: task context, might sleep.
  *
- * This function is just like usb_blk_msg() except that it waits in a
- * killable state.
+ * This function is just like usb_blk_msg(), except that it waits in a
+ * killable state and there is no limit on the timeout length.
  *
  * Return:
  * If successful, 0. Otherwise a negative error number. The number of actual

The patch addresses a vulnerability in the USB core's synchronous API functions (`usb_control_msg`, `usb_bulk_msg`, `usb_interrupt_msg`) that allowed unlimited timeout durations using uninterruptible waits, potentially causing indefinite task hangs with no kill mechanism other than device disconnection. The fix enforces a maximum timeout limit for these non‑killable waits and clarifies timeout parameter semantics.

## Modifications per file

### `include/linux/usb.h`
- Added a new macro `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` with value `60000` (60 seconds). This constant caps the timeout for synchronous USB calls that use uninterruptible waits.

### `drivers/usb/core/message.c`
1. **Timeout logic change** (`usb_start_wait_urb`):
   - For **non‑killable** waits, if `timeout` is `<= 0` or exceeds `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT`, it is clamped to `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` (60000 ms).
   - The jiffies conversion now uses `timeout > 0 ? msecs_to_jiffies(timeout) : MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT`. This means negative values and zero now behave the same as the maximum allowed timeout (instead of infinite). For killable waits, the original behavior (negative/zero → infinite) is preserved.

2. **Comment updates** in several function documentations:
   - `usb_control_msg`, `usb_control_msg_send`, `usb_control_msg_recv`, `usb_interrupt_msg`, `usb_bulk_msg`: removed the phrase “(if 0 the wait is forever)” from the `@timeout` description, replaced with a generic “timeout in msecs to wait before timing out”.
   - `usb_bulk_msg_killable`: explicitly notes that for killable waits there is **no limit** on the timeout length (since they can be killed by a signal), and that the function is similar to `usb_bulk_msg` but with a killable wait.

## Relationships between changes
- The macro `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` defined in the header is used **only** in `usb_start_wait_urb()` within `message.c` to enforce the 60‑second cap for non‑killable synchronous transfers.
- The timeout clamping logic directly prevents indefinite hangs: a caller specifying an excessive or zero/negative timeout will have it automatically set to the maximum (60 seconds) when the wait is uninterruptible. This eliminates the “wait forever” scenario for non‑killable calls.
- The documentation updates align the comments with the new behavior, removing outdated claims that zero means “wait forever” and clarifying the difference between killable (no limit) and non‑killable (capped) variants.

## Summary of Patch Modifications

This patch limits the maximum duration of unkillable synchronous USB operations (e.g., `usb_control_msg`, `usb_bulk_msg`, `usb_interrupt_msg`) to 60 seconds, preventing indefinite hangs that could trigger the kernel's hung-task detector. It also clarifies the behavior of non-positive timeout values.

### Modifications in Each File

**1. `include/linux/usb.h`**
- Added a new macro `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` with value `60000` (milliseconds). This defines the upper bound for timeout values in synchronous USB API calls.

**2. `drivers/usb/core/message.c`**
- **`usb_start_wait_urb()`**:  
  - Added logic before computing the jiffies timeout: for non-killable waits, if `timeout <= 0` or `timeout > USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT`, the timeout is forced to `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT`.  
  - Updated the computation of `expire` to treat positive values as milliseconds, while 0 (or negative after capping for killable) still results in `MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT` (for killable waits only).  
  - Added a comment explaining the enforced maximum for non-killable waits.

- **Documentation updates** in `usb_control_msg()`, `usb_control_msg_send()`, `usb_control_msg_recv()`, `usb_interrupt_msg()`, and `usb_bulk_msg()`:  
  - Removed the phrase "if 0 the wait is forever" and replaced it with "timeout in msecs to wait for the message to complete before timing out". This reflects that 0 or negative values now result in the capped maximum timeout (60 seconds).

- **`usb_bulk_msg_killable()`**:  
  - Updated its documentation: for killable waits, if `timeout <= 0`, the wait is as long as possible (no cap). Also corrected a typo ("usb_blk_msg" → "usb_bulk_msg").

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` macro defined in `usb.h` is the single constant used in `message.c` as the cap for unkillable timeouts.
- The changes to `usb_start_wait_urb()` directly implement the new timeout limit using that macro.
- The documentation updates in all affected functions consistently describe the new behavior: non-positive or excessive timeouts are clamped to the maximum (60 seconds) for unkillable calls, whereas killable calls remain unconstrained (can still wait forever).
- The patch distinguishes between killable and non-killable waits: only non-killable (uninterruptible) timeouts are capped to avoid unkillable tasks; killable waits (like `usb_bulk_msg_killable`) are explicitly left without a limit, as they can be interrupted.

## Summary of the Patch

The patch addresses a vulnerability where synchronous USB message APIs (`usb_control_msg`, `usb_bulk_msg`, `usb_interrupt_msg`) could cause a task to hang indefinitely in an uninterruptible wait due to unlimited timeout durations. The fix introduces a maximum timeout limit for non‑killable waits and clarifies the handling of invalid timeout values.

### Modifications per File

**1. `include/linux/usb.h`**
- Added a new macro definition:  
  `#define USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT 60000 /* ms */`  
  This sets the maximum allowed timeout (60 seconds) for synchronous API calls that use uninterruptible waits.

**2. `drivers/usb/core/message.c`**  
- **`usb_start_wait_urb()`** (the common wait function for all synchronous transfers):  
  - Added a check for non‑killable waits: if `timeout <= 0` or `timeout > USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT`, the timeout is capped to `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT`.  
  - Adjusted the conversion to jiffies: `expire = (timeout > 0) ? msecs_to_jiffies(timeout) : MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT;`  
  - This ensures that a non‑killable wait never uses an unlimited schedule timeout or an excessively long one.  

- **Documentation updates**:  
  - Removed the ambiguous phrase “if 0 the wait is forever” from the kernel‑doc comments of `usb_control_msg`, `usb_bulk_msg`, `usb_interrupt_msg`, `usb_control_msg_send`, and `usb_control_msg_recv`.  
  - For `usb_bulk_msg_killable`, the comment was updated to explicitly state that when `timeout <= 0` the wait is “as long as possible” and that *no limit* applies to killable waits.

### Relationship Between Modifications

- The macro `USB_MAX_SYNCHRONOUS_TIMEOUT` defined in the header is the constant that enforces the timeout cap in `usb_start_wait_urb()`.
- The core logic change in `usb_start_wait_urb()` ensures that all non‑killable synchronous calls (which all go through this function) respect the new maximum, preventing indefinite hangs.
- The documentation changes clarify the new behavior for both capped (non‑killable) and unlimited (killable) variants, making the API contract explicit.
- The overall effect is a safety net: the kernel will never let a synchronous USB transfer with an uninterruptible wait block for more than 60 seconds, while killable waits (like `usb_bulk_msg_killable`) remain fully under the caller’s control.

Here is the commit message:
USB: core: Limit the length of unkillable synchronous
 timeouts

The usb_control_msg(), usb_bulk_msg(), and usb_interrupt_msg() APIs in
usbcore allow unlimited timeout durations.  And since they use
uninterruptible waits, this leaves open the possibility of hanging a
task for an indefinitely long time, with no way to kill it short of
unplugging the target device.

To prevent this sort of problem, enforce a maximum limit on the length
of these unkillable timeouts.  The limit chosen here, somewhat
arbitrarily, is 60 seconds.  On many systems (although not all) this
is short enough to avoid triggering the kernel's hung-task detector.

In addition, clear up the ambiguity of negative timeout values by
treating them the same as 0, i.e., using the maximum allowed timeout.
